newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore PM unveils cabinet after election win.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PM unveils cabinet after election win.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong announced his cabinet on Saturday after being swept back to power in general elections this month in which his party won all but two seats in parliament.
Only four cabinet jobs were changed and Goh brought no new faces into his senior team, shuffling portfolios among existing ministers, according to a statement from the prime minister's office.

Political observers said the limited changes after Goh's January 2 election victory, which was the best result for the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) in 16 years, would leave general policy direction unaltered.
The opposition's number of seats in parliament was cut from four to two.
One Western diplomat in Singapore told Reuters the cabinet changes were "even more limited than I was expecting -- all the major players are pretty much in place."
The lack of new blood in the cabinet underscores Goh's assertion since the election win that he has the right team in place to take his country into the 21st century.
The key change is the high profile Trade and Industry Ministry to which former Education Minister Lee Yock Suan is appointed.
Lee led the team which won a fierce battle against the opposition Workers' Party in the hotly-contested Cheng San Group Representation Constituency.
Cheng San became the focus of the election campaign after Goh accused an opposition candidate there of "Chinese chauvinism" which he said threatened the island's racial harmony.
The former trade minister, Yeo Cheow Tong, takes back the Health Ministry in the reshuffle and is also given the Environment portfolio.
Former Environment Minister Teo Chee Hean takes over at the Education Ministry, vacated by Lee.

In the only other change of cabinet responsibilities, George Yeo relinquishes the Health brief to become Second Minister at the Trade and Industry Ministry. He retains the job of Minister for Information and the Arts.

The statement said there would be a further cabinet change within two years to enable the ministers for communications and national development to remain in post during the implementation of major programmes.
No details were given of what these changes would be.
The statement said the government swearing-in ceremony would be on Saturday January 25 at 12 noon at City Hall Chamber.
